title.en: What flexible hours would mean here

situation.de: Im Einzelgespräch bittet dich die Teamleitung, deinen Vorschlag zur Arbeitszeit zu erläutern.
situation.en: In a one-to-one meeting your manager asks you to explain your working-hours proposal.

sceneCaption.de: Im Einzelgespräch bittet dich die Teamleitung, deinen Vorschlag zur Arbeitszeit zu erläutern. „유연 근무제를 원하신다고 들었는데, 정확히 어떤 걸 말씀하시는 거예요?“
sceneCaption.en: In a one-to-one meeting your manager asks you to explain your working-hours proposal. “유연 근무제를 원하신다고 들었는데, 정확히 어떤 걸 말씀하시는 거예요?”

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 유연 근무제를 원하신다고 들었는데, 정확히 어떤 걸 말씀하시는 거예요?

base.de: Ich habe gehört, dass Sie sich eine flexible Arbeitszeitregelung wünschen. Was genau verstehen Sie darunter?
base.en: I heard you'd like flexible working hours. What exactly do you have in mind?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 제가 말하는 유연 근무제는 하루 여덟 시간은 그대로 일하되 모두 모이는 시간을 열한 시부터 세 시까지로 정하는 방식이에요.

base.de: Mit flexibler Arbeitszeit meine ich, dass ich weiter acht Stunden am Tag arbeite, aber alle nur von elf bis drei gleichzeitig da sein müssen.
base.en: By flexible hours, I mean I’d still work eight hours a day, but everyone would only need to be in together from eleven to three.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 저는 아무 때나 나와서 일도 덜 하는 걸로 알았어요. 시간은 안 줄어드는 거죠?

base.de: Ich dachte, Sie kommen dann irgendwann und arbeiten auch weniger. Die Stundenzahl sinkt also nicht?
base.en: I took it to mean coming in whenever you like and working less as well. You're saying the hours wouldn't be reduced?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 정확히 말하면 유연 근무란 출퇴근 시각만 옮기는 것을 뜻해요. 한 시간 늦게 오면 퇴근도 한 시간 늦어져요.

base.de: Genauer gesagt bedeutet flexible Arbeitszeit, dass sich nur der Arbeitsbeginn und das Arbeitsende verschieben. Wenn ich eine Stunde später anfange, gehe ich auch eine Stunde später.
base.en: To be precise, flexible working means shifting only your start and finish times. If I start an hour later, I finish an hour later too.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그럼 아홉 시에 고객 통화가 잡힌 날은 어떻게 하실 거예요?

base.de: Was würden Sie dann an einem Tag machen, an dem ein Kundengespräch um neun angesetzt ist?
base.en: Then what would you do on a day when there's a client call at nine?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 그런 날은 당연히 아홉 시에 맞춰 나와요. 고객 일정이 먼저지, 제 출근 시간이 먼저는 아니에요.

base.de: An solchen Tagen bin ich natürlich um neun da. Der Kundentermin hat Vorrang vor meiner gewünschten Anfangszeit.
base.en: On those days I'd come in for nine, of course. The customer's schedule takes precedence over my preferred start time.

base.en: It doesn't cut out all the time, just during video calls. To be precise, the picture freezes about three minutes after I switch the camera on.

base.en: So the office connection was fine. It works again as soon as I turn the camera off, so the problem seems to occur only when I'm sending video.

base.de: Sie sagten „bis Freitag“, also habe ich die Datei am Freitagabend um elf geschickt. Ich war etwas überrascht, dass das zu spät gewesen sein soll.
base.en: You said “by Friday”, so I sent it at eleven on Friday night. I was a bit surprised to hear it was late.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 제가 말한 금요일까지는 금요일 밤이 아니라 아침 열 시 회의 전이었어요. 제가 시각을 따로 말했는지 저도 다시 확인해 볼게요.

base.de: Mit „bis Freitag“ meinte ich nicht Freitagnacht, sondern vor der Sitzung am Freitagmorgen um zehn. Ich schaue selbst noch einmal nach, ob ich die Uhrzeit ausdrücklich angegeben habe.
base.en: By “Friday” I meant before the ten o'clock meeting on Friday morning, rather than Friday night. I'll check whether I actually specified the time.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 메시지를 다시 봤는데 금요일까지라고만 적혀 있었어요. 회의 얘기는 없었고요.

base.de: Ich habe die Nachricht noch einmal gelesen. Da stand nur „bis Freitag“. Von der Sitzung war keine Rede.
base.en: I've checked the message again. It just said “by Friday”. There was no mention of the meeting.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 그러면 그건 제 잘못이에요. 머릿속으로는 회의 전을 생각했는데 글로는 날짜만 쓴 거죠.

base.de: Dann war das mein Fehler. Im Kopf hatte ich „vor der Sitzung“, aber geschrieben habe ich nur das Datum.
base.en: Then that was my fault. I had “before the meeting” in mind, but I only wrote the date.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그럼 앞으로 마감을 어떻게 적으면 서로 헷갈리지 않을까요?

base.de: Wie könnten wir die Frist künftig so angeben, dass es für uns beide eindeutig ist?
base.en: How should we write deadlines from now on so neither of us is left guessing?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 다음부터는 날짜랑 시간을 같이 쓸게요. 예를 들면 금요일 아침 열 시 회의 전까지, 이렇게요.

base.de: Künftig schreibe ich Datum und Uhrzeit zusammen. Zum Beispiel „vor der Sitzung am Freitagmorgen um zehn“, so in der Art.
base.en: From now on I'll put the date and time together. For example, “before the ten o'clock meeting on Friday morning”, like that.

base.en: You mentioned a neighbourhood gathering the other day. I heard they meet every week. What kind of gathering is it exactly?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 단골 모임이라고 해요. 예를 들면 매주 목요일 같은 식당에 자주 오는 사람들이 따로 약속하지 않아도 자연스레 모이는 거예요.

base.de: Man nennt das ein Treffen der Stammgäste. Zum Beispiel kommen Leute, die oft in demselben Restaurant essen, jeden Donnerstag von selbst zusammen, auch ohne sich eigens zu verabreden.
base.en: People call it a regulars' gathering. For example, people who often eat at the same restaurant naturally meet there every Thursday without making a special arrangement.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그럼 동호회 같은 거네요? 회원 명단 있고 회비도 내는 그런 거요?

base.de: Dann ist das wie ein Freizeitverein? Mit Mitgliederliste und Beitrag?
base.en: So it's like a hobby club, with a membership list and dues?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 동호회라기보다는 약속 없이 만나는 이웃 모임에 가까워요. 명단도 없고 회비도 없고, 그냥 그 시간에 오면 되는 거죠.

base.de: Eher ein Nachbarschaftstreff ohne Verabredung als ein Freizeitverein. Es gibt weder eine Liste noch Beiträge. Man kommt einfach um die übliche Zeit vorbei.
base.en: It's closer to neighbours meeting without an appointment than to a hobby club. There's no list and no fee. You just turn up at the usual time.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그러면 누가 한 달 동안 안 나오면 어떻게 돼요? 뭐라고 안 해요?

base.de: Und wenn jemand einen Monat lang nicht kommt? Sagt da niemand etwas?
base.en: What happens if someone doesn't come for a month? Doesn't anyone say anything?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 아무도 안 물어봐요. 다시 오면 그냥 자리를 내주는 거고요, 그게 이 모임의 핵심이에요.

base.de: Niemand fragt nach. Wenn die Person wiederkommt, macht man ihr einfach Platz. Genau das macht das Treffen aus.
base.en: Nobody asks about it. When they come back, you just make room for them. That's the heart of the gathering.

base.en: You're here because of headaches? Please describe how it hurts.

dialogue.targetText: 아픈 부위는 머리 전체가 아니라 오른쪽 눈 뒤쪽이에요. 구체적으로는 일주일에 서너 번씩 그쪽이 지끈거려요.

base.en: The painful area is behind my right eye rather than my whole head. More specifically, it throbs there three or four times a week.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 세기보다는 시간이 중요해요. 보통 하루 중 언제 시작해서 얼마나 가나요?

base.de: Der Zeitpunkt ist wichtiger als die Stärke. Wann beginnt der Schmerz normalerweise und wie lange hält er an?
base.en: The timing matters more than the intensity. When during the day does it normally start and how long does it last?

dialogue.speaker: you

base.de: Sie möchten ein Regal nach Maß bestellen? Welche Abmessungen stellen Sie sich vor?
base.en: You're looking to order a made-to-measure bookshelf, right? What size did you have in mind?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 높이는 이 미터, 폭은 팔십 센티미터고요, 깊이는 사십 센티미터면 좋겠어요. 선반 높이도 나중에 바꿀 수 있을까요?

base.de: Zwei Meter hoch und achtzig Zentimeter breit. Vierzig Zentimeter Tiefe wären gut. Könnte ich die Höhe der einzelnen Böden auch später noch verändern?
base.en: Two metres high and eighty centimetres wide. I'd like it forty centimetres deep. Would I also be able to change the shelf heights later?

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 선반은 구멍 뚫어서 옮기게 할 수 있어요. 그런데 깊이는 보통 삼십이 기본이에요. 사십은 왜 필요하세요?

base.de: Wir können Löcher für verstellbare Böden bohren. Bei der Tiefe sind allerdings dreißig Zentimeter üblich. Wofür brauchen Sie vierzig?
base.en: We can drill holes so you can adjust the shelves. But the standard depth is thirty centimetres. Why do you need forty?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 서류 상자가 들어가야 하거든요. 상자가 삼십육이라서 삼십이면 앞으로 튀어나와요. 그러니까 기본이 아니라 사십이어야 해요.

base.de: Meine Aktenboxen müssen hineinpassen. Sie sind sechsunddreißig Zentimeter tief und würden bei dreißig vorne überstehen. Deshalb brauche ich vierzig, statt des Standardmaßes.
base.en: My file boxes have to fit. They're thirty-six centimetres deep and would stick out at the front on a thirty-centimetre shelf. That's why it has to be forty, rather than the standard depth.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그러면 뒷판을 더 두꺼운 걸로 써야 해서 값이 이십 퍼센트쯤 올라가요. 괜찮으세요?

base.de: Dann brauchen wir allerdings eine dickere Rückwand. Dadurch wird es ungefähr zwanzig Prozent teurer. Ist das in Ordnung?
base.en: Then we'll need a thicker back panel, so the price will go up by about twenty percent. Is that okay?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 네, 상자가 들어가는 게 더 중요하니까 추가 비용은 괜찮아요. 깊이 사십에 두꺼운 뒷판으로 해 주세요.

base.de: Ja, mir ist wichtiger, dass die Boxen hineinpassen. Den Aufpreis akzeptiere ich. Bitte vierzig Zentimeter tief mit der dickeren Rückwand.
base.en: Yes, it's more important that my boxes fit, so the extra cost is fine. Please make it forty deep with the thicker back panel.

dialogue.speaker: them

base.de: Der Hinweis zur Mülltrennung hier ist für mich etwas schwierig. Was heißt „nicht recycelbar“?
base.en: I'm finding the waste-sorting sign here a bit difficult. What does “not recyclable” mean?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 이 사무실 분리배출 안내문에서 재활용 불가는 재활용 통이 아니라 일반 쓰레기로 버리라는 뜻이에요. 쉽게 말하면 저기 흰 봉투에 넣으라는 거죠.

base.de: Auf dem Schild hier im Büro bedeutet „nicht recycelbar“, dass es in den Restmüll gehört und nicht in die Recyclingtonne. Einfach gesagt soll es dort in den weißen Sack.
base.en: On this office's sorting sign, “not recyclable” means dispose of it with ordinary rubbish instead of in the recycling bin. In plain words, put it in that white bag.

dialogue.targetText: 아, 저는 아예 버리면 안 되고 따로 모아 둬야 하는 줄 알았어요.

base.de: Ach, ich dachte, man dürfe es gar nicht wegwerfen und müsse es getrennt aufbewahren.
base.en: Oh, I thought you weren't allowed to throw it out at all and had to keep it separate.

dialogue.speaker: them

base.de: Den Begriff gibt es bei uns nicht. Was macht man bei einer Retrospektive?
base.en: We don't use that term in my field. What do people do at a retrospective meeting?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 저희 팀에서 회고는 지난 작업에서 뭐가 잘됐고 뭐가 아쉬웠는지 돌아보는 회의예요. 프로젝트가 끝날 때마다 한 시간쯤 해요.

base.de: In unserem Team ist die Retrospektive ein Treffen, bei dem wir auf die letzte Arbeit zurückblicken. Was lief gut, was hätte besser laufen können? Wir nehmen uns nach jedem Projekt etwa eine Stunde dafür.
base.en: In our team a retrospective is a meeting where we look back on what went well and what could have gone better. We spend about an hour on it at the end of each project.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그러면 결국 누가 잘못했는지 따지는 자리 아니에요? 그런 회의는 다들 싫어할 것 같은데요.

base.de: Geht es dann letztlich darum, wer etwas falsch gemacht hat? Solche Besprechungen mag doch sicher niemand.
base.en: So isn't it ultimately about finding out who did something wrong? I can't imagine people liking meetings like that.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 아니에요, 누가 잘못했는지 찾는 게 아니라 다음에 뭘 바꿀지 정하는 자리예요. 사람 이름은 아예 안 나와요.

base.de: Wir suchen keinen Schuldigen. Wir legen fest, was wir beim nächsten Mal ändern. Namen kommen gar nicht vor.
base.en: No, it's a meeting to decide what to change next time, rather than find out who's at fault. People's names don't come up at all.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그럼 실제로 어떻게 진행되는지 예를 하나만 들어 주시겠어요?

base.de: Könnten Sie mir ein konkretes Beispiel dafür geben, wie so etwas abläuft?
base.en: Could you give me one example of how it works in practice?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 예를 들면 마감이 늦었으면 왜 늦었는지 보고, 다음부터는 검토 기한을 이틀 앞당기기로 정하고 끝나요. 그게 전부예요.

base.de: Wenn wir zum Beispiel eine Frist verpasst haben, sehen wir uns den Grund an. Am Ende vereinbaren wir etwa, die nächste Prüffrist um zwei Tage vorzuziehen. Das ist schon alles.
base.en: For example, if we missed a deadline, we look at why, then wrap up by agreeing to move the review deadline two days earlier next time. That's all there is to it.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 팀장님한테 그 프로젝트 반대하신다고 전했어요. 회의에서 그렇게 말씀하셨잖아요.

base.de: Ich habe der Teamleitung gesagt, dass Sie gegen das Projekt sind. Das haben Sie doch in der Sitzung gesagt.
base.en: I told the team lead that you oppose the project. That's what you said at the meeting, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 제가 말한 취지는 그게 아니에요. 제가 반대한 건 일정이지 프로젝트 자체가 아니거든요. 한 달만 미루자는 거였어요.

base.de: Darauf wollte ich nicht hinaus. Ich habe den Zeitplan abgelehnt, nicht das Projekt an sich. Ich wollte es nur um einen Monat verschieben.
base.en: That wasn't my point. I objected to the schedule, not the project itself. I was only suggesting pushing it back by a month.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그래도 저는 분명히 지금은 안 된다고 하시는 걸 들었어요. 그게 반대 아니에요?

base.de: Aber ich habe deutlich gehört, dass Sie gesagt haben, jetzt gehe es nicht. Ist das kein Widerspruch gegen das Projekt?
base.en: But I distinctly heard you say it couldn't go ahead now. Doesn't that mean you oppose it?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 지금은 안 된다는 말은 맞아요. 그런데 그건 시기 문제지 하지 말자는 뜻은 아니에요. 하되 늦게 하자는 거죠.

base.de: Dass es jetzt nicht geht, habe ich gesagt. Aber das ist eine Frage des Zeitpunkts. Ich habe nicht vorgeschlagen, es sein zu lassen. Ich möchte es durchaus durchführen, nur später.
base.en: I did say we couldn't do it now. But that's about the timing, not a call to drop it. I'm saying we should go ahead, just later.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그럼 팀장님께 제가 다시 전할 수 있게 한 문장으로 말씀해 주시겠어요?

dialogue.speaker: you

base.en: I support the project and think only its start should be postponed until next month. You can put it to them that way.

sceneCaption.en: A community-centre employee wants a clear account of the street festival's traffic plan. “부스는 열 시에 연다고 들었는데, 차량 통행은 어떻게 되는지 순서대로 설명해 주시겠어요?”

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 부스는 열 시에 연다고 들었는데, 차량 통행은 어떻게 되는지 순서대로 설명해 주시겠어요?

base.de: Ich habe gehört, dass die Stände um zehn öffnen. Könnten Sie mir Schritt für Schritt erklären, wie der Verkehr geregelt wird?
base.en: I heard the booths open at ten. Could you walk me through what happens to traffic?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 순서대로 말씀드리면 열 시부터 정오까지는 평소대로 다녀요. 정오부터 다섯 시까지는 일반 차량을 막고, 우회로는 바로 옆길이에요. 다섯 시에 다시 열려요.

base.de: Der Reihe nach. Von zehn bis zwölf fließt der Verkehr wie gewohnt. Von zwölf bis fünf sperren wir die Straße für normale Fahrzeuge. Die Umleitung führt über die Straße gleich daneben. Um fünf öffnen wir wieder.
base.en: In order, traffic runs as usual from ten until noon. From noon to five we close the road to ordinary vehicles and divert them to the street alongside it. The road reopens at five.

dialogue.speaker: them
dialogue.targetText: 그런데 한 시쯤에 구급차가 지나가야 하면 어떻게 돼요? 그때는 길이 막혀 있을 텐데요.

base.de: Was passiert, wenn gegen eins ein Rettungswagen durchmuss? Dann ist die Straße doch gesperrt.
base.en: But what if an ambulance needs to get through around one? The road will be closed then.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.targetText: 그건 괜찮아요. 남쪽 입구는 하루 종일 비상 차로로 비워 두거든요. 막는 건 일반 차량이지 구급차는 아니에요.

base.de: Das geht trotzdem. Die südliche Zufahrt halten wir den ganzen Tag als Rettungsgasse frei. Gesperrt ist die Straße für normale Fahrzeuge. Krankenwagen dürfen durch.
base.en: That's fine. We keep the south entrance clear as an emergency lane all day. The restriction is on ordinary vehicles, so ambulances can still get through.

dialogue.speaker: them
